# Adding a "Delete My Account" Button (Flask + SQLite) Here's a complete implementation covering the backend route, database cleanup, and frontend button with a confirmation dialog. ## 1. Backend Route ```python from flask import Blueprint, render_template, redirect, url_for, flash, request from flask_login import login_required, current_user, logout_user from werkzeug.security import check_password_hash from app import db from app.models import User, Post, Comment # adjust to your models @bp.route("/account/delete", methods=["GET", "POST"]) @login_required def delete_account(): if request.method == "POST": # Require password confirmation for safety password = request.form.get("password", "") if not check_password_hash(current_user.password_hash, password): flash("Incorrect password. Your account was not deleted.", "error") return redirect(url_for("account.delete_account")) user = current_user # 1. Handle related data # Option A: cascade delete via ORM relationships # (configure relationships with cascade="all, delete-orphan") # # Option B: delete explicitly Post.query.filter_by(user_id=user.id).delete() Comment.query.filter_by(user_id=user.id).delete() # 2. Log out BEFORE deleting the user object logout_user() # 3. Delete the user db.session.delete(user) db.session.commit() flash("Your account has been permanently deleted.", "success") return redirect(url_for("main.index")) # GET → show confirmation page return render_template("account/delete_account.html") ``` ## 2. Deletion Template `templates/account/delete_account.html` ```html {% extends "base.html" %} {% block content %}

Delete My Account

This action is permanent and cannot be undone. All your data, including posts and comments, will be erased.

Cancel
{% endblock %} ``` ## 3. Button in Your Profile Page `templates/account/profile.html` ```html Delete my account ``` ## 4. Optional: Cascade in Models To avoid manual deletes, define cascades in your models: ```python class User(db.Model, UserMixin): # ... posts = db.relationship("Post", backref="author", cascade="all, delete-orphan") comments = db.relationship("Comment", backref="author", cascade="all, delete-orphan") ``` Then the backend route only needs `db.session.delete(user); db.session.commit()`. ## 5. If You Use Foreign Keys Without ORM Cascades SQLite doesn't enforce `ON DELETE CASCADE` unless PRAGMA is enabled. Ensure it is: ```python from sqlalchemy import event @event.listens_for(Engine, "connect") def set_sqlite_pragma(dbapi_connection, connection_record): cursor = dbapi_connection.cursor() cursor.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON") cursor.close() ``` ## Checklist Before Shipping - ✅ **CSRF protection** — the form includes `csrf_token` (Flask-WTF). - ✅ **Password re-entry** — prevents accidental/malicious deletion. - ✅ **`logout_user()` before delete** — avoids stale session referencing a deleted user. - ✅ **Related data handled** — nothing orphaned in the DB. - ✅ **Confirmation dialog** — a `confirm()` prevents accidental clicks; use a modal if you prefer. - ✅ **GDPR/CCPA note** — keep a record of deletion requests if required by your jurisdiction. - ✅ **Audit log (optional)** — log `"user X deleted account"` before deletion, storing only a hash of the user ID.
